text:
Alyssa: Heads up — I'm seeing a weird eviction/wear pattern in the KV cache for long-context runs on Llama-MQA variants when rope scaling > 1.0 is enabled. Repro is fairly stable on a local perf harness. Memory climbs steadily and we start thrashing pages after ~180k tokens.

Kevin: ugh. any logs or pprof traces? :eyes:

Alyssa: Yep. Attached the minimal repro command and the pprof flame snippet (pasted). It looks like eviction is repeatedly removing pages that were just populated by the same request stream (hot pages), then the next batch fetches them again. That suggests reuse detection isn't matching due to rope-scale-induced key offsets.

Alyssa: Repro command:
```
# run long context with rope scaling and MQA-enabled model
./perf_harness --model llama-mqa-7b --rope-scale 1.25 --tokens 200000 --batch 8 --kv-pool-size 64G --evict-policy lru-ish
```

Alyssa: Key snippet from the heap/kv pprof (flame condensed):
```
[CPU]  42% runtime:kv_lookup
  -> kernel:kv_page_read 28%
  -> kernel:kv_evict_write 12%
[MEM]  growing allocations in kv_page_slot (hot)
  -> page_refcount churn around same page ids
```

Shreya: Interesting. Could be index normalization when rope-scale != 1.0. We normalize positions into the kv index; if the normalization math is different for MQA vs GQA that'd explain mismatched keys and hence duplicate pages (different keys for same logical context). Have you dumped key fingerprints?

Alyssa: I did a quick dump of the first 10k slots: same logical positions produce two different key hashes depending on whether MQA patch ran path A or path B (kernel selection changed because of small seq-len heuristic). I can paste a small table but it's noisy.

Ivan: We merged a kernel-selection tweak last week that prefers the 'aligned-page' kernel for seq_len >= 512. That kernel changed internal slot base offset by +8 to align for AVX kernel tiling. If rope-scale causes effective positions to shift, the base-off-by-8 could produce different slot addresses.

Kevin: So two interacting things: kernel picks different offset + rope-scaling changes indices -> same logical key maps to two physical slots -> fragmentation and repeated eviction/repopulation. Makes sense.

Shreya: If that's the case, we need a deterministic canonicalization step for the kv key that happens before kernel-specific offseting or else kernel selection must guarantee identical mapping. Quick mitigation: disable the new aligned-page kernel for MQA models or force a canonical pre-offset when computing key fingerprints.

Alyssa: I ran with the aligned kernel forced off and the growth goes away. Token throughput drops ~6% but steady memory and no thrash. Repros with the aligned kernel on show page churn numbers x3.

Kevin: Can you paste the small reproducer log showing slot ids? That will help Shreya / Ivan confirm the +8 effect.

Alyssa: Pasted cropped sample below (slot_id, fingerprint):
```
# seq_pos  slot_id_before  slot_id_after  fingerprint
1024      0x7f12ab00      0x7f12ab08     abcd1234
1025      0x7f12ab40      0x7f12ab48     abcd2345
...
```

Alyssa: Notice the after values are consistently +0x8 when aligned kernel chosen. Fingerprints correspond to different canonical keys, so we treat them as distinct.

Ivan: Yep that's the +8. I think the kernel was doing a micro-optimization (pad for vector loads) but forgot to apply the same pad to the fingerprint canonicalization step. That's a bug.

Shreya: Patch idea: compute canonical_fingerprint = hash(key_base + rope_normalized_pos) before any kernel-local alignment. Then kernel can apply local padding only to physical layout, not to the canonical id. I'll write a quick RFC.

Alyssa: Thanks. Also note this only showed up with MQA and when rope_scale != 1.0. GQA runs didn't hit it because the earlier codepath forces a single kernel variant and avoids the aligned kernel.

Kevin: For short-term: add a scoring/detection heuristic in runtime that detects high page churn (evict_count/page_repop > threshold) and logs a warning + auto-fallback to non-aligned kernel for that model. Could reduce incidents in prod.

Shreya: Agreed. I'll prototype the canonicalization patch + a unit test that asserts identical fingerprints across kernel selection path for multiple rope_scale values.

Alyssa: CI run I'm referencing: https://ci.internal/runs/4129 (failed when aligned kernel on). Includes perf flame and kv churn dashboards.

ci-bot: Build 4129 status: failed — 1 test failed (kv_fingerprint_consistency). See: https://ci.internal/build/4129/logs

Ivan: I'll open the kernel patch PR to remove the implicit padding in fingerprint path and add a comment. Shreya, if you add the unit, we can run the MQA/GQA matrix with rope_scale {0.8,1.0,1.25}.

Alyssa: Sounds good. After the patch I want to rerun long context 200k token runs overnight to confirm no mem climb. I'll also add a small runner that records evict_count/repop_count per-minute.

Kevin: Nice debugging. This is a good example of cross-cutting perf: kernel selection + runtime keying + model-format (MQA) interacting. :thumbsup:

Shreya: I'll drop the RFC & unit test PR today. Ivan, ping me when kernel PR is up and I'll review.

Alyssa: TY all. Leaving logs in the thread and will update with overnight run results. :rocket:
